template.name: Mindray BeneFusion SP1 Vet Syringe Pump
template.desc: Mindray BeneFusion SP1 veterinary syringe pump. Class I, internally powered, IP34, defibrillation-proof type CF applied part (syringe) (ops manual H-046-022424-00 v2.0 A.1.1, p. A-1). Service manual H-046-022454-00 v1.0 chapter 3 tests patient leakage through an applied-part connection tooling, so a CF applied part “Syringe” on RA, patient leakage and mains on applied parts were added (Ansur had none). From the CHS Ansur template “0000 Benefusion SP1 0000000000 Vet EST+PVT AS-NZS 3551 DD.MM.YYYY.mtt”. Electrical safety to AS/NZS 3551:2012+A2. Changed from Ansur: earth leakage NC 5000, ON 10000 µA (B11.6) (Ansur: NC 500, ON 1000 µA); enclosure leakage NC 100, ON 500, OE 500, RNC 100, RON 500, ROE 500 µA (Ansur: no limits). Changed from Ansur: occlusion pressure at the Medium level is 400–650 mmHg (ops manual 5.2.1 and A.5: 525 ± 125 mmHg; Ansur 420–705 mmHg in its text and 56–94 kPa as the limit, a typo); readings are in mmHg. Changed from Ansur: power-on and operational checks added from service manual 3.3 and 3.5; duplicate power-on items and the misplaced power-on item in the visual check removed; calibrations are due-only and N/A otherwise; maintenance passwords removed. Kept as in Ansur, differs from the manual (for Jonathan to confirm): enclosure leakage single fault 500 µA (service manual 3.6.1: 300 µA); there is no earth leakage test in the manual. Kept as in Ansur (unverified): volume set-points (10 mL 100 mL/h 5 mL; 20 and 30 mL 200 mL/h 10 mL; 50 mL 500 mL/h 25 mL; limits ±2 %, matching the ±2 % in ops A.5) and pressure test at 100 mL/h; the SP1 service manual has no performance test.

items: The housing is clean, without scratches, assembled firmly, and there is no abnormal noise when the pump is shaken
The display, keys, power cord and accessories have no obvious damage
The external connecting cables are not frayed, and the connectors are firm with no loose or bent pins
The labels and data plate are complete, correct and legible
Press the power switch: the System Self-test screen is displayed
The buzzer and the speaker each sound during the self-test (service manual 3.3: buzzer first, then speaker)
The alarm lamp changes from red to yellow, then goes out
Battery: disconnect the AC supply briefly; the pump keeps running on the battery
The indicator lamp gives normal prompts for battery charging and discharging

steps.title: Mains voltage
steps.instructions: Plug the ESA612 into the mains supply you are testing from.

steps.title: Protective earth resistance
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an exposed earthed metal part, such as a rear-panel screw.

steps.title: Insulation: mains to non-earth accessible conductive part
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet and switch the device on. Don’t touch the device during the test.

steps.title: Enclosure leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. Clip the red test lead to an unearthed part of the enclosure (the service manual wraps metal foil on the housing and connects the applied part to RA).

steps.title: Earth leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the device’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet. The device will be switched on and off between conditions.

steps.title: Patient leakage
steps.instructions: Connect the applied part to the RA post: the syringe, through the applied-part connection tooling or metal foil wrapped round a filled syringe barrel (service manual: SUM end of the tooling to RA). Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet.

steps.title: Mains on applied parts
steps.instructions: Connect the applied part to the RA post: the syringe, through the applied-part connection tooling or metal foil wrapped round a filled syringe barrel (service manual: SUM end of the tooling to RA). Connect the pump’s mains lead to the ESA612 equipment outlet.

steps.title: Operational Test
steps.instructions: Service manual 3.5 (pages 3-6 and 3-7). Install a syringe and use test water.

items: Each key operates normally in line with the user manual, and no abnormal operation makes the pump crash
Sound and light alarms at every level are normal, the volume control works and the alarm mute works
After an alarm is triggered, the operation and the alarm are recorded in the history
Install the syringe, set the infusion parameters and press Start: the Run screen is displayed, and the running icon, rate, accumulated volume and pressure are normal

steps.title: Performance Test
steps.instructions:
Calibration: service manual 3.4 (pages 3-3 to 3-6; due at least every two years, with a new syringe brand, after maintenance or an upgrade, or if the flow is doubtful). The user and factory maintenance passwords are in the service manual.
Volume performance test: this manual gives no volume test; the set-points are CHS's (as in the Ansur template), and the limits are the ±2 % infusion accuracy in ops manual A.5. Fill each syringe with clean water, set the rate and preset volume below, start into a clean empty container and stop when the Complete alarm sounds. Weigh the water on a balance (the Ansur text said 0.1 g; use a finer balance if you have one). 1 g of water = 1 mL.
Occlusion pressure test: this manual gives no pressure test; the set-point is CHS's and the limit is the Medium level, 525 ± 125 mmHg, in ops manual 5.2.1 and A.5. Fill the syringe and an extension tube with water and connect them to a pressure analyser (Fluke) in blocking test mode. Set the occlusion pressure to Medium and 100 mL/h, start, and read the maximum pressure when the Blocking alarm sounds. Press to cancel the alarm.

items: Syringe calibration (service manual 3.4.1; 5, 10, 20, 30 and 50 mL standard syringes): Calibration Completed. N/A if not due
Pressure calibration (3.4.2; Fluke at 300 mmHg and 900 mmHg): Calibration Completed. N/A if not due
Sensor calibration (3.4.3; standard components 13.5 mm and 32 mm): Calibration Completed, and the displayed outer diameter is close to the 32 mm component. N/A if not due
